brief: Morgan Stanley frames four 2026 midterm takeaways. First, tariffs, trade, deregulation, immigration and export controls stay with the executive branch regardless of outcome; the only real fiscal variance is the timing of SNAP/Medicaid cuts, defense spending and shutdown/debt-limit severity, and the deficit stays near 6% of GDP in every scenario with only small (~0.2pp) swings. Second, midterms are not a 2028 signal (the president keeps veto power, and only two of six midterm-to-presidential issue pairs since 1994 carried their top-ranked issue forward), but four debates - social security, individual taxes (the CA wealth tax), data center restrictions and healthcare - reveal where 2028 fault lines are forming. Third, election outcomes drive AI sentiment through two vectors: data center opposition (a clear catalyst, most constructive for sentiment under a Republican sweep, least under a Democratic sweep) and AI safety/regulation (not a key driver, since comprehensive legislation needs a high-salience incident). Fourth, market impact concentrates in sectors and Treasury supply rather than the macro outlook: a Republican sweep cheapens the belly and lifts the dollar, a Democratic sweep removes upside risk to Treasury borrowing needs, and a fragile Democratic majority brings the least supply pressure but the clearest growth downside.
